title: Dedicated tenant snapshot service for residency evidence
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a service that generates cryptographically verifiable on-demand and scheduled snapshots of Dedicated tenant allocation and runtime metadata to serve data residency and tenant-isolation attestations. The snapshot must be compact, privacy-preserving (no PII or request payloads), signed by the customer KMS/HSM or our signing key per contract, and exportable as an evidence bundle consumable by auditors.
acceptance_criteria: API to request an on-demand snapshot for a tenant returns a signed bundle with index and metadata within SLA (target 120s for typical 10-node tenant).
Scheduled monthly snapshots are stored in tenant-specific object prefixes with retention TTL honoring tenant retention settings.
Bundle format documented: index.json, node-manifests/*.json, cryptographic-signature.sig, and an obfuscated-claims.md explaining what was excluded.
Snapshots do not include request payloads, customer data, or logs containing PII; a scanner validates bundle contents before signing.
Evidence bundles verifiable offline using published verification tool and public key; sample verification in repo with integration tests.
Operational dashboard tile shows last snapshot time, generation duration, bundle size, and last verification status.
Security review completed and KMS/HSM signing keys provisioned for dedicated tenants who opted-in.
design_decisions: Use a pull-based snapshot generator that queries the orchestration layer for current allocation, network tags, and node metadata to avoid coupling with live request paths.
Represent ephemeral runtime state as hashed digests (SHA-256) of node descriptors instead of raw kernel logs to reduce sensitive exposure.
Bundle signing will support two modes: customer-managed KMS (preferred) and Redwood-managed key for tenants without KMS. All keys will be backed by HSM in both modes.
Store bundles in an immutable object-store prefix with append-only metadata ledger entries (ledger rows include bundle key, signer key ID, and timestamp) to support audit trails.

To avoid high load on production nodes during large snapshot generation, perform data collection from the orchestration control plane and cached node-state exporter rather than directly streaming from each tenant VM/container.
implementation_notes: Service: tenancy-snapshotter (new microservice) written in Go, exposes REST + internal gRPC for orchestration calls.
Collector: reuse existing node-state-exporter but extend to provide signed digests and per-field redaction rules.
Signer integration: wrap KMS operations in signer facade; implement transparent retries and idempotency tokens to avoid double-signing bundles.
Preflight scanner: runs content validation against allow-list/deny-list to ensure no PII; implemented as a separate binary to keep signing path minimal.
Performance: snapshot generation should be CPU- and IO-capped (cgroups) and run on dedicated control-plane nodes to isolate tenant load.
Backfill: provide migration job to generate snapshot archives for tenants who enabled residency attestation in last 12 months (rate-limited).
testing_plan: Unit tests for bundle encoder/decoder, index schema validation, and preflight scanner rules.
Integration test that requests on-demand snapshot against a staging dedicated cluster and verifies signature and manifest structure.
Fuzz tests for manifest fields to ensure verifier rejects malformed bundles.
Load test: simulate 200 concurrent snapshot requests (sized to typical 10-node tenant) and confirm controller QoS and overall system stability.
Penetration test focused on signer key handling and bundle storage access control (coordinate with security team).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable snapshot API for internal test tenants and run daily scheduled snapshots for 2 weeks; monitor CPU, storage growth, and preflight false positives.
Phase 2: Opt-in release to a handful of beta customers (3-5 tenants) with signed bundles delivered to their S3 prefix.
Phase 3: General availability for all Dedicated tenants with opt-in in Console and API; migration job to generate recent historical snapshots for tenants that opt-in during onboarding.
Rollback: if preflight scanner produces >2% false positives or a signer failure pattern emerges, disable automated scheduling and open a mitigation ticket; maintain manual export path until fix.
